IO3_transformations.algorithm: Verify creator has permission (founder/admin/mod). Insert into group_channels table. Initialize message thread. Add channel to group sidebar.
Verify member has access to channel. Encrypt message. Insert into messages table with channel_id. Broadcast to members.
On emergency: create #emergency-updates (read-only, admins post), #shelter-locations (curated), #help-needed (members post requests). Auto-pin to top.
IO3_transformations.accuracy_target: All channels created, pinned, members can see immediately

DW1_upstream_pipeline.description: Member joins group. Can see all non-private channels.
Member creates channel or posts message

DW2_downstream_pipeline.description: Verify user has permission to create channel (founder/admin/mod) or post (member+)
Channel created in group_channels table. Message inserted into messages table.
New channel appears in all members' channel list (real-time). Message appears in thread (real-time).
Channel creation and admin actions logged

P.P1_bottleneck_analysis: Channel list updates to many members (fan-out on new channel). Message broadcasting (real-time sync). Emergency channel auto-creation coordination (many groups simultaneously). Private channel access control (permission checks on message fetch).
P.P2_defensibility: Default #general channel provided (no empty groups). Private channels prevent off-topic spam. Auto-emergency channels are system-provided (consistent, reliable). Channel-level mute enables filtering.
P.P3_confidence_level: Very high confidence. Channel system is straightforward CRUD with broadcast. No novel complexity.
P4_failure_modes: Channel creation fails → group stuck with only #general (mitigate: retry, system admin override)
Emergency channels not created → admins can't post official updates (mitigate: alert admins, manual creation option)
Message not broadcast → member sees old message list (mitigate: retry broadcast, user refresh)
Private channel access leaked → member sees private channel they shouldn't (mitigate: permission check on every fetch)
P.P5_backup_plan: If channel creation fails: retry. If emergency channels fail: manual creation. If broadcast fails: async retry. If private access fails: deny access, log incident.
P.P6_backup_plan_test: Simulate channel creation failure. Test emergency channel auto-creation failure. Test broadcast failure (disconnect network). Test private channel access edge cases.
P.P7_testing_strategy: Unit tests for channel creation logic. Integration tests for permission checks. Load tests for channel list broadcast (10k members, new channel). End-to-end tests for full channel workflow (create, post, read). Emergency channel tests (verify creation, permissions, pinning). Private channel tests (verify access control).
P.P8_benchmarks: Channel creation: <200ms. Message post: <500ms. Broadcast: <2s for 10k members. Emergency channel creation: <10s for all channels. Private access check: <50ms. Channel list update: real-time (WebSocket) or <5s (polling). False positive (wrong member sees private channel): 0%.

L.L1_legal_considerations: Channels enable moderation (off-topic in dedicated channels). Private channels prevent unintended disclosure. Auto-emergency channels ensure official information visible (legal authority). Channel history may be subpoenaed (retention policy needed).
L.L3_consent_requirements: Implicit consent by joining group and using channels.
L.L4_liability_notes: Private channel message leakage could expose sensitive data. Mitigation: strict permission checks. Off-topic discussion in wrong channel could spread misinformation. Mitigation: channel descriptions, moderation tools.

F.F1_cost_considerations: Channel metadata: ~200B per channel. Message storage: same as DMs (~500B per message). At 100k groups with 5 channels each, 500k channels. Minimal storage overhead.
F.F3_revenue_impact: Channels improve group organization and engagement (retention). Positive impact.

S.S1_cybersecurity: Private channels require permission check on every access (no caching of public/private status). Channel list visible only to members (no enumeration of private channels from outside). Rate limiting on channel creation (prevent spam).
S.S2_data_privacy: Channel names visible to all group members. Channel descriptions visible to members. Private channel existence hidden from non-members. Message encryption same as DMs.
S.S3_encryption_requirements: Messages encrypted same as DMs: Signal Protocol or AES-256-GCM
S.S4_access_control: Public channels visible to all members. Private channels require permission (set by creator). Only permitted members can read private channel messages. Founder/admin can view all channels.
S.S5_audit_requirements: Log channel creation and deletion. Log permission changes (public to private, etc). Log moderation actions (message removal, member removal). Audit trail retention: 1 year.

X.X1_notes: Channels are essential for group organization. Default #general prevents empty groups. Private channels enable confidential discussions. Auto-emergency channels ensure consistent official communication during crises. Channel-level mute prevents notification spam.
